status: Qualified native three-file persistence and menu/R/L controls; production Phone remains disabled
scope: Isolated synthetic native battery files only. Ordinary title/file-selection controls choose native indices 0, 1 and 2 (visible files 1, 2 and 3); no selected/loaded-file memory injection.

Qualified preboot startup is native 316 with three CPUs in 801, unchanged retail geometry/source assignments, synthetic identity, experimental Phone enabled, Area Keys ON, ability gating OFF and health minimum 6/maximum 10.
Only production validated ROM/health pairing, complete-history handling and Phone/Copy ownership synchronizers perform grants. No live AP server or full game watcher is involved.

All gameplay observations are checkpoints, not per-frame traces. The player is Normal with HP 6. No mid-run state loads or direct writes to pose, equipment, battery or Phone/Copy ownership fields are used.
The foreign ROM changes only the 16 synthetic identity bytes. It loads a separate copy of the canonical battery; the canonical input remains unchanged.

The separately labeled Area Key arrival control uses the existing production runtime configurator with synthetic precollection bit 16. It is separate from the ten guarded ownership-queue writes in the grant matrix.
findings: File 0 grants Phone then Copy, producing ownership bits 2 then 3. File 1 grants Copy then Phone, producing bits 1 then 3.
File 2 remains unowned before its own grant, then receives Phone only (bits 2). The canonical final battery has ownership bits 3, 3 and 2.
All six redundant WORLD checksums validate in every accepted output, and both copies agree on identity and ownership.
Initial blank-save boot initializes all three native WORLD ranges. Subsequent matrix transitions change only the selected file range.

Three offline cold loads independently retain the expected bits 3, 3 and 2, perform no client writes and leave the entire 32768-byte battery identical. They restart this fixture in 316; no retail tutorial or Central Circle reset claim is made.
A foreign-identity load clears both ownership bits in selected file 1 only. Files 0 and 2 remain byte-for-byte unchanged and no client writes occur.

With complete synthetic Phone/Copy histories, both production ownership synchronizers reject three menu attempts: file selector, file 0 mode menu and file 2 mode menu after Back/navigation. Context remains inactive; no queue write or save change occurs.

In the unowned file 2 R control, a 60-frame hold preserves battery 3/caller 255. In owned files 0, 1 and 2, the same hold consumes one battery and enters caller 0. L then returns each case to 801 with retained ownership and subsequent movement.
A matched same-ROM/save/input file-2 control changes only production Area Key configuration from zero to Mustard bit 16: all helpers arrive in 316 by the 600-frame checkpoint only in the keyed run.
limits: The original four no-key R controls certify initiation/battery/return only. The separate matched Area Key control below isolates the missing key in file 2 and records arrival, without certifying a helper target, route, all three files or arbitrary state.
No arbitrary health, copy ability, source assignment, RoomSanity, enemy timing, multiplayer, full watcher or native BizHawk Lua guarantee follows.
Menu WORLD previews are not gameplay ownership evidence. Native selected, active and loaded IDs are compared only after actual gameplay starts.

One preliminary harness used the Copy serial field as its slot assertion and stopped before any writes; that failed attempt is excluded. Successful cases require complete settled/control checkpoints, not merely a runtime file written by cleanup.

area_key_arrival_control.qualification: Matched file-2 cold runs use the same ROM, persisted Phone save, controller inputs and two-frame post-config wait. Production _sync_area_key_runtime_config receives starting_area_key_bitfield 0 versus 16 after ROM/health validation and complete synthetic history. The keyed run makes one ordinary four-byte runtime configuration write, not a guarded ownership-queue write. No pose, equipment, AI or direct Phone/Copy ownership field is written.
area_key_arrival_control.result: Both R holds consume one battery. At 600 and 1800 post-R frames the zero-key CPUs remain in 801 while all keyed CPUs are in 316. L returns the local player to 801 in both cases. This isolates the Mustard Key configuration in this qualified fixture, not universal helper cooperation or target activation.
